current.summary: One open living and dining room. The wall between the old lounge and the top-of-stairs passage has been taken down (marked on the plan), so the room now runs through to the back doors in the angled side wall. The flat ceiling has been removed: what you now see is the roof itself — dark timber beams and rafters with a boarded deck of weathered planks, sloping down at the dining end. Along the walls are the cut-off stubs of the old attic-floor joists, at the old 2.42 m ceiling height. On the angled side the walls step up in white masonry: a deep niche used as a daybed, and above it a high ledge — the last piece of the old attic floor — with the small attic window. Sitting area: grey sofa (2.1 m) facing the TV. Dining end: dark extendable table with green velvet chairs, a tall dark-wood dresser/plate rack (used for wine and display), and two old built-in cupboards painted olive green — one with glazed doors (china), one panelled (tools/storage now). Also: antique wooden bar counter, gilt mirror over a wrought-iron wine-rack console, exposed brick panel. Floor: large light-grey tiles. Lighting: glass-drop chandelier, black cage pendants on long flexes, cage wall light.

Pendant flexes looped across beams; mixed light fittings (crystal / black cage / gilt)

Damaged/patched skirting with black membrane showing beside the back-door recess — check for damp
Grey tile + grey sofa read cold against the warm timber

target.concept: DRAFT for discussion — let the roof lead. Warm lime-white walls with their soft texture so the dark beams, the weathered boards and the brick panel do the talking. GREEN IS ALREADY THE HOUSE'S THREAD — the old cupboards, the outside of the front doors, the kitchen units, the velvet chairs — so make it deliberate: restore the two built-in cupboards in one chosen historic green and pick that same family for the daybed bolsters. Build the niche into a proper daybed, make the high ledge a lit display shelf, put the lighting into one warm family (aged brass, linen) with uplights washing the boards, and warm the floor with a large earth-toned rug under the sofa.
